newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KLINSMANN TO LEAVE BAYERN AND GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN TO LEAVE BAYERN AND GERMANY.

text.p: Juergen Klinsmann is to give up a lucrative contract at Bayern Munich after a troubled season and will end his top-flight career outside Germany.

The 32-year-old striker shocked German soccer on Tuesday when he announced he was leaving Bayern at the end of the season, saying he did not fit in at the Bundesliga's richest but most controversial club.

Klinsmann, who is giving up one of the biggest pay packets in German football worth around $3 million a year, will definitely leave the Bundesliga although he has yet to decide where he will be playing next season. Spain or England appear the most likely possibilities.

Klinsmann, who captained Germany to victory at last year's European championship, returned to his homeland in 1995 after an enjoyable period at London side Tottenham where he was voted England's Footballer of the Year and was a hugely popular figure with the fans.

The move to Bayern was expected to be the last major transfer of his career. But, despite helping the team to win the UEFA Cup last season, things have not worked out at a club which has a reputation for dressing-room battles.
Klinsmann complained earlier in the season that he was unhappy with Bayern's defensive tactics and the way he had been treated when he went through a bad patch.
On Tuesday he told reporters he would not be completing his contract which runs until the end of next season.
"I had a talk with (chairman) Franz Beckenbauer last week and I told him that I would probably play abroad next season," he said. "I don't fit in here.
"I wanted to tell Bayern now so that they can plan for the future. There are many reasons (why I am leaving) and I have decided to act."

During his time at Bayern, Klinsmann has often been at odds with club captain Lothar Matthaeus, his predecessor in charge of the national team. He has found it difficult to cope with the squabbling which is part of everyday life at the club.
"It was obvious that the whole ballyhoo in Munich got on Juergen's nerves," Bayern general manager Uli Hoeness said. "He has said that himself many times."

The atmosphere was very tense in Munich last week after two bad defeats. It has emerged that Beckenbauer told the team that they were a poor side during a special meeting and was also very critical in public.
Beckenbauer, who played a key role in bringing Klinsmann back to Germany, said: "It's a shame. We wanted to keep Juergen a lot longer. But it's his personal decision and we have to accept it."
One of Klinsmann's lowest moments came at the end of last year when he was substituted in a key league match at his old club VfB Stuttgart where he made his name in the German game.
Shortly afterwards Klinsmann, who struggled to score goals in the first half of the season, threatened to leave Bayern.
Klinsmann can leave before the end of his contract in June 1998 since he has an opt-out clause which allows him to quit without a transfer fee.

Several English clubs are believed to be interested in signing him but he is also believed to have had offers from Spain. In addition to Tottenham, Klinsmann has played for France's Monaco and Italy's Inter Milan.
The decision will add an extra incentive to Bayern's attempts to lure VfB Stuttgart's Brazilian striker Giovane Elber to Munich for the start of next season.
